# Part 5 — Field Operations


> **About this draft.** Written for **CSRs**, not for Field Ops technicians. The question it answers is what a CSR needs to know about Field Ops to handle a call well — what's happening to the order, what the patient was told, what the documents mean, and when to transfer.
>
> Escalation targets render as the current role holder, linked to the escalation directory. Figure placeholders mark images to be added.

## §5-1 Scope and routing

Field Operations owns everything **after an order is validated**: scheduling, delivery, technician setup, equipment pick-up, and service dispatch.

### §5-1.1 Two queues

| Queue | Handles |
|---|---|
| **Field Ops Q** | Delivery scheduling, pick-up scheduling, service visit scheduling, delivery status |
| **Field Ops-Power Q** (ext 344) | Power-related scheduling — delivery, ATP evaluations and PMD service visits — as well as PMD Order Verification |

### §5-1.2 Field Ops or Service?

| Situation | Where it goes |
|---|---|
| Validated (<img class="ico" alt="Authorized" src="data:image/png;base64," width="64" height="64">) but not delivered | Field Ops |
| Delivered (<img class="ico" alt="Delivered" src="data:image/png;base64," width="64" height="61">) and the caller says the delivery was wrong | **Service**, not Field Ops |
| Delivered same day with something missing or wrong, no <img class="ico" alt="Delivered" src="data:image/png;base64," width="64" height="61"> yet — the missing Delivered icon is the difference from the row above | Field Ops is usually better suited |
| Shipped package the carrier shows as delivered, but the patient says it never arrived | **Service** — a lost-package claim, [[§6-2]] |
| Mask fitting | Field Ops Q |
| Equipment fault after delivery | Service |

## §5-2 Is the order in Field Ops?

If a transaction is **validated** (<img class="ico" alt="Authorized" src="data:image/png;base64," width="64" height="64"> under `Trx State`) but **not delivered** (no <img class="ico" alt="Delivered" src="data:image/png;base64," width="64" height="61"> under `Ticket State`), it is likely in the Field Ops grid. Full icon legend at [[§0-10.1]].

To confirm:

| Check | Where |
|---|---|
| Delivery notes | `Notes` tab — look for delivery-related entries |
| Delivery ticket artifact | `Artifacts` — has a delivery ticket been uploaded? |
| Date scheduled | `Ticket` tab, top of page |
| Route information | `Ticket` tab, bottom — Stop # / Total (helps narrow the expected delivery window) |
| Tracking numbers | `Ticket` tab — double-check for multiple tracking numbers and shipper info; track each and advise on the ETA accordingly |

## §5-3 Routing rules for common calls

| What the notes or caller says | What to do |
|---|---|
| "Calling to schedule on [date], no answer, left message" | If the patient or caregiver is calling **back in response to that message**, transfer to Field Ops so they can officially schedule based on current availability. Do not confirm the date yourself and notify Field Ops afterward — availability may have changed since their note |
| Field Ops is trying to get a discharge date | Confirm the D/C date with the caller — scheduling cannot proceed without it. Note the D/C date and who is confirming it, then transfer to Field Ops or email the details |
| Delivery date noted as "verified via documentation" | Officially scheduled. Payment can be processed from the `Patient Responsibility` tab — check for secondary insurance first, see [[§10-20.1]] |
| Patient in a SNF with no D/C date | Cannot schedule. See [[§5-4]] |
| Patient in an Assisted Living Facility (ALF) | No D/C date required — an ALF generally qualifies as the patient's home. Can transfer to Field Ops to schedule |
| PMD delivery date and notes date differ by 1–3 days | Technicians cover large areas within date ranges. Treat the date mentioned in the notes as the official scheduled date |
| Caller verifying a D/C date that matches what's listed | If the notes show it's already scheduled for that D/C date, note the account and email or chat Field Ops. No transfer needed |
| Secondary insurance found mid-fulfillment | Add the details and update the notes, then transfer to Field Ops to update and resume accordingly |
| Freight company calling about a delivery | Get the company name and the city they're delivering to, then transfer to **Field Ops-Power** and relay both |

## §5-4 Delivery to a facility

The rules here come from Medicare and they constrain what Field Ops can schedule. A CSR who knows them can explain a delay instead of escalating it.

### §5-4.1 The two-day rule

> **Policy — pre-discharge delivery.** Equipment may be delivered to a patient in a hospital or nursing facility **no earlier than two days before discharge**, and only for the purpose of fitting or training.
>
> - The **date of service is the discharge date**, not the delivery date
> - The patient must take the item home, or UMS collects it and delivers to the home on the discharge date — **at no charge to the patient**
> - Discharge must be to a qualified place of service — home or custodial — not to a hospital or skilled nursing facility (one that isn't the patient's home)
>
> Full billing detail is in [[§10-13.3]].

> **Watch-out — a delayed discharge breaks it.** The two-day window is firm. If the discharge date moves, the item has to be picked up and redelivered within two days of the new date. This is why Field Ops will not schedule against an unconfirmed discharge date, and why a patient whose discharge slipped may see their delivery reset.

### §5-4.2 SNF, ALF, and why the answer differs

| Facility type | Qualifies as the patient's home? | Effect |
|---|---|---|
| Hospital | No | Pre-discharge rule applies; D/C date required |
| Skilled nursing facility (SNF) | No | Pre-discharge rule applies; D/C date required. **Also a coverage question** — see below |
| Assisted living facility (ALF) | Generally yes | No D/C date needed; schedule normally |

> **Policy — a SNF is more than a scheduling problem.** During a Medicare **Part A covered SNF stay**, consolidated billing makes the facility responsible for the patient's DMEPOS, and UMS cannot bill Medicare for it regardless of the discharge date. A confirmed D/C date does not by itself make a delivery payable.

If a caller is in a SNF and pushing for delivery, the answer is that we need the confirmed discharge date before scheduling — and that the patient's equipment during the stay is the facility's responsibility.

### §5-4.3 Supplies are excluded

> **Policy** — Supplies cannot be shipped until the patient is discharged. The pre-discharge rule covers durable medical equipment — including prosthetics and orthotics — **not supplies**. There is no two-day window for them.

### §5-4.4 PMDs are not delivered to a medical facility

> **Policy** — A power mobility device cannot be delivered to a hospital, rehab facility or SNF — though it can be delivered to a nursing home that is the patient's permanent residence. It is delivered to the patient's home by a UMS technician, and **the patient must be present** so the technician can adjust the device and instruct them in its use.

### §5-4.5 Texas Medicaid delivery timing

An unlikely situation, but worth knowing: for a Texas Medicaid client, equipment delivered too early isn't reimbursed — and can't be recovered.[^txmd]

[^txmd]: Equipment is not reimbursed if it is delivered before the prescribing provider's signature date on the Title XIX order form, or more than three business days before TMHP prior authorization is obtained. All DME purchased for a Medicaid client becomes the client's property upon receipt — including in both of those situations. The DME Certification and Receipt Form must also be completed before reimbursement for any DME delivered to a Texas Medicaid client.

## §5-5 What happens on an in-person delivery

Useful when a patient asks what to expect, or calls afterward disputing what happened.

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| Advance call | The driver or technician calls the patient or caregiver **30–60 minutes before arrival** to say they're en route |
| Setup | For equipment requiring assembly, the technician builds it on site |
| Instruction | For PMDs, the technician adjusts the device and instructs the patient in its use |
| Documentation | The patient (or a designee) and the technician sign the delivery documents — see [[§5-6]] |

### §5-5.1 Hospital beds — clearing space

> **Policy — the patient must clear the space.** Field Ops advises the patient or caregiver in advance that space needs to be cleared for the technician to build the bed.
>
> **Technicians cannot move personal items.** This is a liability restriction, not a preference. If the space is not clear on arrival, the build may not be able to proceed.

> **Script — setting the expectation.** "Before the technician arrives, you'll want to have the area where the bed is going cleared out — furniture, boxes, anything in the way. Our technicians aren't able to move personal belongings, so having that ready makes sure the setup can proceed smoothly without needing to reschedule."

### §5-5.2 PMD delivery photos

Technicians will often — though not always — photograph the device after delivery, and sometimes with the patient seated in it. This confirms the delivery was accepted and the equipment arrived in good condition.

If a patient later disputes the condition of the device or claims it was never delivered, check `Artifacts` for delivery photos before escalating.

## §5-6 Delivery documents

Three documents come out of a delivery, and patients call about all three.

### §5-6.1 Proof of Delivery (POD)

POD is what proves the patient received the item. Without it, the claim cannot be paid.

> **Policy — required on every POD.** Patient's name, delivery address, a description of the item (narrative, HCPCS code, or brand and model), quantity delivered, date delivered, and the signature of the patient or their designee.

| Rule | Detail |
|---|---|
| Who may sign | The patient, or a designee. A designee **may not be anyone with a financial interest**. If the signature isn't legible, the name is noted on the slip, and the designee's relationship to the patient should be recorded |
| Date entry | The date may be entered by the patient, the designee, or the supplier — but if the document carries both a supplier-entered date and a patient signature date, **the patient-entered date takes priority** |
| Shipped items | Carrier tracking documentation serves as POD, linked to the UMS shipping record — also found in `Patient Artifacts` |
| Retention | **Seven years** from the date of service |

`[FIGURE: delivery ticket — example for reference]`

### §5-6.2 Delivery ticket

Every delivery includes a signed acknowledgment from both the technician and the patient. This is the record a CSR checks when a delivery is disputed.

### §5-6.3 Purchase Capped Rental Form (PRF)

> **Policy — this is what answers the "nobody told me" call.** The PRF is signed by the patient at delivery and acknowledges Medicare's billing procedure for **capped rental** items as distinct from **routinely purchased** items.

Patients frequently call to complain that no one explained the 13-month rental billing. The signed PRF is how UMS supports the position that they were in fact informed.

> **Watch-out** — Check `Artifacts` for the signed PRF before conceding the point on a call. Confirming the patient wasn't told, when a signed form exists, undercuts the company's position on a billing dispute.

> **Script — patient says they were never told about the 13 months.** "I understand — dealing with insurance can be overwhelming. Let me walk you through how it works. Your insurance rents the equipment for a 13-month period, and after that it's yours and the rental billing stops. There's a form covering this that's signed at delivery, and I can see it on your account. If you'd like a copy, I'd be more than happy to email it to you securely."

The billing rule itself is in [[§10-13.1]].

## §5-7 Failed and rejected delivery

| Situation | What happens | CSR action |
|---|---|---|
| Nobody home | The technician cannot complete the delivery, and leaves a notice on the front door. Field Ops reschedules | Note the account, transfer to Field Ops to reschedule |
| Space not cleared for a hospital bed | Build may not proceed — see [[§5-5.1]] | Explain the requirement and reschedule through Field Ops |
| Patient refuses the delivery at the door | The patient may reject a delivery if unsatisfied. Nothing is billed | Note the reason. Route to the department queue to determine whether the order is changed or closed |
| PMD and the patient isn't home | Cannot be delivered — the patient must be present. See [[§5-4.4]] | Reschedule through the Field Ops-Power Q |
| Wrong address | Delivery cannot complete | Confirm and update the address per [[§0-3.1]], then Field Ops reschedules |

## §5-8 Shipped deliveries and resupply

### §5-8.1 Resupply shipping windows

{{diagram:resupply-windows}}

> **Policy — Medicare timing limits.** The patient must confirm they need the refill **within the 30 days** before their current supply runs out, and UMS may ship **no sooner than 10 days** before it runs out.
>
> For a shipped order, the **shipping date** is the date of service — not the day it arrives. A shipment that leaves within the 10-day window is compliant even if it lands a few days later.

This is the answer to "why can't you just send it now." It isn't a UMS preference — shipping early makes the claim non-payable.

> **Script** — "Insurance sets the window for when we can send the next shipment — we're not able to ship earlier than the allowed timeframe before you run out, per insurance guidelines. I'll follow up with that team to make sure it goes out as soon as possible."

For PAP patients there's a second gate: resupply also requires documented ongoing use and a doctor visit within the required timeframe. A patient out of compliance cannot receive supplies until it's resolved — see [[§3-7.4]].

### §5-8.2 Emergency overnight shipping

Possible for respiratory supplies if the patient pays the difference in shipping cost. Contact `[ROLE: Field Operations Supervisor]`.

## §5-9 Pick-up procedures

When creating a pick-up ticket, tell the caller you are creating a ticket that Field Operations will review, and that Field Ops will verify it and **call back within 24–48 hours** to confirm **if and when** pick-up can happen.

Field Ops reviews **every** pick-up ticket and decides whether anything more is needed — documents from the MDO, for example.

> **Watch-out — never promise a pick-up.** Pick-up is not always possible.

### §5-9.1 When pick-up may not happen

| Reason | Example |
|---|---|
| Same or Similar consequences | A hospital bed with 10 of 13 months paid — picking it up doesn't reset anything, and the patient will likely have difficulty getting another hospital bed through insurance for five years from the original delivery under the SOS rule. See [[§10-13.5]] |
| Mostly paid for | If the equipment is nearly paid off, waiving the remaining balance can be the better outcome than recovering it. Field Ops decides — see [[§10-15.1]] |
| Patient-owned | After ownership transfers at month 14, the item is the patient's and is not picked up |

> **Note — tell the patient what a pick-up means.** Mention that they'll likely have difficulty getting similar equipment through insurance within the next five years, so they can make an informed decision. Some callers ask us to pick up equipment they own anyway — we can't, because it's now their private property, but they're free to donate or dispose of it.

### §5-9.2 PMD pick-up requests

Clarify the reason before creating anything:

{{diagram:pmd-pickup}}

| Reason given | Action |
|---|---|
| Uncomfortable, or it sounds adjustable | **Transfer to Service.** Do not create a pick-up ticket — fit problems are often adjustable |
| Technical fault | **Transfer to Service** for repair. Do not create a pick-up ticket |
| Cannot afford it | Offer the **EAA or a payment plan** first — [[§5-9.3]]. Neither is available on an out-of-pocket order |
| None of these, and the item is patient-owned | It can't be picked up — it's theirs to keep, donate or dispose of. See [[§4-9.1]] |
| None of these, and not patient-owned | Create the pick-up ticket |

> **Watch-out — a pick-up may be irreversible, so present the options first.** A patient who surrenders a PMD may have difficulty obtaining another for five years under the Same or Similar rule ([[§10-13.5]]). Ask what's actually wrong before treating it as a return, and offer the EAA or a payment plan **before** creating a ticket when cost is the reason. Patients often change their mind about a pick-up once they've heard all of their options.

### §5-9.3 Economic Assistance Application (EAA)

Two options exist for a patient who cannot pay the full amount, and both let them keep the equipment rather than surrender it:

| Option | Set up by |
|---|---|
| **Economic Assistance Application (EAA)** | Processed by **Billing**. A CSR or Billing sends the patient the blank form — see below |
| **Payment plan** | The **Billing team** — transfer or route the request to them |

> **Policy — out-of-pocket orders qualify for neither.** A patient without insurance can still purchase equipment from us, but an **OOP order is ineligible for the EAA and for a payment plan**. Don't offer either on an out-of-pocket purchase.

**How the EAA works**

| Step | Detail |
|---|---|
| 1 | A CSR or the Billing team sends the patient the **blank EAA form** — it's in the CSR shared drive, or in the UMS App under `Admin` → `Service Provider Forms` |
| 2 | The patient completes it — monthly income, expenses and related financial information — and returns it to us |
| 3 | The completed form goes to **Billing**, who process it |
| Turnaround | No set timeframe — usually **within 1–2 weeks** |

### §5-9.4 What goes in a pick-up ticket

| Field | Why |
|---|---|
| Reason | Deceased, moved, no longer needed, non-compliance, supplier change |
| Best contact, pick-up address, and access instructions | Field Ops has to reach someone and get in |

> **Policy** — Billing uses the pick-up date to end the rental, so the date has to be accurate. See [[§10-15]].

`[FIGURE: pick-up ticket creation — from the tutorial slideshow]`

## §5-10 Hospital bed relocation

Patients frequently ask us to move a delivered hospital bed from one location to another.

> **Policy — we generally do not relocate hospital beds.** The exception is a patient in the **Dallas, San Antonio, or Hawaii** areas who is moving to another location **within the same area**. Even then:
>
> - The bed must still be a **rental**. A patient-owned bed (month 14+) is not ours to move
> - There is a **$150 charge**
> - A supervisor needs to approve — either a Field Ops supervisor or a Service supervisor can decide. **Route the call to Service**

If it's approved, the path is **Service ticket created → validated by the Service team → pushed to Field Ops for scheduling**. There are two teams in that path, so it isn't a same-day answer — tell the caller it's being evaluated, not that it's being arranged.

> **Script — patient asking to move a bed.** "Relocating a bed isn't something we're usually able to do. There are a few areas where it may be possible if you're moving within the same region, and there's a $150 charge for it. Let me check if this case is eligible."

A patient moving **out of the service area**, while the bed is still in the rental period and not yet paid off, is a different situation — the rental may end and the equipment be picked up. See [[§10-15]].

## §5-11 Manufacturer backorder

Once an order is verified and approved, Field Ops places it with the manufacturer. The usual ETA depends on the item: a PWC typically takes 2–3 weeks to reach our warehouse ([[§4-9]]); shipped supplies are typically received in 1–3 business days; other items vary. A backorder makes any ETA unpredictable.

> **Watch-out — explaining backorders can be difficult.** The order is approved, the patient has been told it's coming, and nothing on the ticket has changed. If an order seems to have been undelivered for an unusual length of time, check the notes for mention of a backorder before simply telling the caller it's on the way.

| What happens | Detail |
|---|---|
| Recording | The backorder is **stated in the notes**. Check there before explaining a delay |
| Patient contact | **Field Operations proactively contacts and updates the patient** in these situations |
| Substitute model | If a substitute is available, it is offered in that same conversation |
| Timeframe | An estimated timeframe is given **if the manufacturer has relayed one**. If not, we say so plainly rather than estimating |

> **Policy — no invented dates.** If the manufacturer hasn't given us an ETA, tell the patient we haven't received one. Do not construct an estimate from the usual timeframe; a backorder is by definition outside it.

> **Script — patient asking about a backordered item.** "Your order is approved and placed with the manufacturer, but the item is on backorder on their side. Our field operations team is tracking it and will reach out with updates. I don't have an estimated date from the manufacturer yet — as soon as they give us one, we'll pass it on."

> **Script — when an ETA does exist.** "The manufacturer has it on backorder and they're estimating [timeframe]. That's their estimate rather than ours, so it can move, but that's what we've been given."

## §5-12 Used equipment sales

Rare, but possible at a reduced out-of-pocket cost depending on availability. Email `[ROLE: Used Equipment Sales Contact]` with the request.

| Detail | |
|---|---|
| Pool | Limited. Most commonly PWC K0821 and K0823, and CPAP |
| Prescription | Items requiring an Rx for out-of-pocket purchase **still require one** — oxygen concentrators, PAP devices (CPAP and BiPAP), and ventilators. See [[§3-2]] |

---

## §5-13 Upgrade fee returns

> **Policy — refund window.** An order with an upgrade fee paid can be returned **unused within the 15-day return period**, but the **20% restocking fee is non-refundable** from the upgrade fee amount. After 15 days the upgrade fee is **fully non-refundable**.

Upgrade fee amounts and the waiver rules are in [[§10-16]].

---

## §5-14 Freight deliveries

If a freight company or driver calls about a delivery, ask for the **freight company's name** and the **city they're delivering to**, then transfer to **Field Ops-Power**, relaying both.

Irving office freight delivery availability: **Monday–Friday, 9:00 AM – 5:00 PM Central Time**.

---

## §5-15 Oximetry devices

Provided temporarily to gather data rather than as ongoing equipment. **Delivery and pick-up are scheduled simultaneously.**

> **Watch-out** — This makes an oximetry order look wrong in the system: a pick-up appears scheduled while the item doesn't yet show as delivered. That's expected, not an error.

## §5-16 FAQ

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| When is my equipment being delivered? | Check the `Ticket` tab for the scheduled date and route position |
| Why can't you deliver to the nursing home now? | Equipment can only be delivered up to two days before discharge, and we need the confirmed discharge date — if Field Ops is still trying to confirm it, that's the blocker. During a Medicare-covered stay the facility is responsible for the patient's equipment. See [[§5-4]] |
| Can you ship my supplies to the hospital? | No. Supplies can't ship until the patient is discharged, and are shipped to the patient's home. See [[§5-4.3]] |
| Why can't you send my supplies early? | Insurance limits how early we can ship — no sooner than 10 days before the current supply runs out. See [[§5-8.1]] |
| Nobody told me about the 13-month billing. | The Purchase Capped Rental Form is signed at delivery and covers it. Check `Artifacts` before conceding. See [[§5-6.3]] |
| Can you move my hospital bed to my new place? | Generally no. Limited exceptions in Dallas, San Antonio and Hawaii for moves within the same area, at $150 and subject to supervisor verification. See [[§5-10]] |
| Can I return this and get the upgrade fee back? | Within 15 days and unused, less the 20% restocking fee. After 15 days the upgrade fee is non-refundable. See [[§5-13]] |
| Will someone call before they arrive? | Yes — the technician calls 30–60 minutes before arrival |
| I can't afford my power wheelchair anymore. | Offer the EAA or a payment plan before anything else — neither is available on an out-of-pocket order. See [[§5-9.3]] |
| I never received my order. | Check `Artifacts` for a signed delivery ticket, or the carrier's proof of delivery for a shipped item, and tell the caller the confirmed POD. See [[§5-6.1]]. A shipped package the carrier shows as delivered that the patient still says never arrived goes to Service — [[§6-2]] |
